proposed_widenings.name: passive_grant family for ClassFeatureMechanics
proposed_widenings.justification: Weapon Mastery is a passive/preparatory feature — it is always-on once configured at level-up or rest. The current surface only has the 'activation' family, which implies a runtime trigger, an activation cost, and a use-count resource. None of these apply. A 'passive' or 'grant_access' family is needed for features that configure a persistent capability rather than triggering an effect.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency

proposed_widenings.name: GrantMasteryAccessEffect (or GrantWeaponMasterySlots) in ClassFeatureEffect
proposed_widenings.justification: The current ClassFeatureEffect union is GrantExtraActionEffect | HealHpEffect. Neither variant models 'unlock use of mastery properties for N chosen weapon kinds'. A new variant is required to represent this access-granting pattern.
proposed_widenings.evidence: you to use the mastery properties of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency

proposed_widenings.name: no_resource (or absent resource) in ClassFeatureMechanicsHeader
proposed_widenings.justification: ClassFeatureMechanicsHeader mandates resource: UseCountResource. Weapon Mastery has no use count — the feature is continuously active. The surface needs either an optional resource field or a 'no_resource' variant to represent passive features without quotas.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Feature text describes no usage limit; the only 'reset' is a reconfiguration of which weapons are chosen, not a count refill.

proposed_widenings.name: reconfigure_on_long_rest cadence in RestResetCadence
proposed_widenings.justification: The existing RestResetCadence variants (short_or_long_rest, long_rest, short_rest, partial_short_full_long) all describe refilling a use-count pool. Weapon Mastery's Long Rest interaction changes which weapon kinds are selected — a reconfiguration, not a refill. This is a structurally distinct operation.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose.

notes: The same structural gap applies to every class's 'Weapon Mastery (class L1)' feature (fighter, barbarian, paladin, ranger, rogue). All share the same passive-grant + long-rest-reconfiguration pattern. The v4 atom 'grant_proficiency' is the closest analogue but is not represented in ClassFeatureEffect. The 'choose' procedure atom (v4 §2) is also unrepresented for the per-rest weapon-kind selection. No honest encoding is possible without adding a passive family and a mastery-access effect variant.
